title: Apply a vCenter resource pool plan and report accurately when a later step fails
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. Build `VcfResourcePoolRollout.psm1` at the workspace root. It applies a resource pool plan to one vCenter, one pool at a time. Rollouts fail part way through often enough that the report matters more than the happy path: when a pool cannot be created, the pools created before it still exist, and whoever picks up the ticket has to be able to tell from the report exactly what is now on the vCenter and what never got attempted.

The runner already installs the PowerCLI SDK modules `VMware.Sdk.vSphere` 13.5.0.25380678 and `VMware.Sdk.vSphereRuntime` 8.0.2099.24145081. Import and use those genuine SDK modules: build the server configuration with `New-vSphereServerConfiguration`, issue every request with `Invoke-vSphereApiClient`, and build the request body with the SDK models `Initialize-VcenterResourcePoolCreateSpec`, `Initialize-VcenterResourcePoolResourceAllocationCreateSpec` and `Initialize-VcenterResourcePoolSharesInfo`. Do not vendor VMware modules or replace the SDK transport with `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Invoke-RestMethod`, curl, raw sockets, `HttpClient`, or another HTTP client.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification, not a documentation page, and not the 9.1 revision of the same file. The only operationIds in scope are `Cis.Session_create`, `Cis.Session_delete`, `Vcenter.ResourcePool_list` and `Vcenter.ResourcePool_create`. The acceptance harness points the real SDK at a contract-pinned loopback vCenter and calls:

`Invoke-VcfResourcePoolRollout -Server <string> -Credential <pscredential> -PlanPath <string> [-SkipCertificateCheck]`

A plan file is JSON. `parentPool` is the name of the pool everything is created under, and `pools` is the ordered list to create. Every pool has a `name`. `cpuAllocation` and `memoryAllocation` are optional, and each may set any of `reservation`, `limit`, `expandableReservation` and `shares`, where `shares` sets `level` and, for a `CUSTOM` level, `shares`:

```
{
  "parentPool": "<pool name>",
  "pools": [
    { "name": "<pool name>" },
    { "name": "<pool name>", "cpuAllocation": { "limit": 8000 },
      "memoryAllocation": { "reservation": 4096, "expandableReservation": false,
                            "shares": { "level": "CUSTOM", "shares": 1500 } } }
  ]
}
```

Requirements:

- Export only `Invoke-VcfResourcePoolRollout`. `Server` is a `host:port` authority, and `SkipCertificateCheck` must reach the server configuration.
- Authenticate once per call with `Cis.Session_create` using the supplied credential over basic auth, present the returned token as `vmware-api-session-id` on every later request, and close the session with `Cis.Session_delete` before returning, including when the rollout stopped on a failed pool. A session teardown that itself fails must not mask the report.
- Resolve `parentPool` to its identifier with `Vcenter.ResourcePool_list`. That operation has six independent `style: form`, `explode: true` filters, so each one is a top level query key; `names` is the only filter this rollout sets, and the other five must contribute no key at all. Fail the run if the name matches no pool or more than one, and name the pool in the error.
- Create the pools with `Vcenter.ResourcePool_create`, in plan order, one request each. The 201 body is the identifier of the new pool.
- Every optional property that was not set must be absent from the request body rather than sent as null or empty. This nests two deep: a pool that tunes no CPU omits `cpu_allocation` entirely, an allocation that sets only a limit carries `limit` alone, and a shares block for a non-`CUSTOM` level carries `level` alone. A plan may also carry an allocation block that sets nothing at all; an allocation with no members is not the same as a default allocation, so it has to be left off the wire too.
- The first failed pool stops the rollout. Do not attempt the pools behind it, and do not try to undo the pools in front of it. vCenter refuses a pool whose name is already taken under the parent, and refuses a reservation larger than what the parent has left to hand out; report whichever came back rather than assuming one of them.
- A failed pool is reported, not thrown: by then the change is partly applied and the record is the point. Only a failure that leaves vCenter untouched, a refused session or a `parentPool` that cannot be resolved, may throw.
- Return one object with properties in this exact order: `Server`, `ParentPoolName`, `ParentPoolId`, `PlannedCount`, `CreatedCount`, `Created`, `Failed`, `NotAttempted`, `Succeeded`. `Created` holds one row per pool that was created, in creation order, each row with properties in this exact order: `Name`, `ResourcePoolId`. `Failed` is `$null` when the whole plan applied, otherwise an object with properties in this exact order: `Name`, `Status`, `ErrorType`, `Message`, carrying the pool name, the HTTP status, the `error_type` discriminator and the `default_message` vCenter returned. `NotAttempted` holds the names of the pools behind the failure in plan order, and `Succeeded` reports whether the whole plan applied.
- The SDK runtime probes a pre-7.0.2 `/rest` endpoint when it is left to discover whether a server needs deprecated APIs. That endpoint is not in the contract, so pin the setting instead of letting it probe.

Acceptance: `pwsh -NoProfile -File verify.ps1`. It uses dummy credentials against `127.0.0.1` only, invokes the genuine VMware SDK, and reads the mock's request log to verify the exact method, target, query key set, request body, session lifecycle, where the rollout stopped, the reported result, and the omission of every unset optional field. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `verify.ps1`, `mock_vcenter.py`, `.gitignore` and everything under `docs/` and `plans/` are protected; do not modify them.
